question: The outermost range of the Himalayas is the Shivalik, which ranges between 900 and 1100 metres in height, and lies in width between ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 and 50 km**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Shiwalik(Outer Himalayas):

 
 
• The **outermost range of the Himalayas is called the Shiwalik(Outer Himalayas.)**
 
• It **extends over a width of 10-50 Km** and has an altitude varying between 900 and 1100 metres.
 
• The **word Shiwalik literally means "tresses of Shiva".**
 
• Shiwalik is** parallel to the Ganga plain.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The word Himalaya means "the abode of snow".
 
• The Himalaya is mostly formed of sedimentary rocks.
 
• The Himalayas consist of three main parallel ranges, namely:
 
 
• The greater Himalayas.
 
• The lesser Himalayas.
 
• The outer Himalayas.
